answer: Require each agent identity to earn trust slowly, like a glacier: reputation accrues only from attested work over time, never from a self-declared name. A Sybil farmer can spawn ten thousand sock puppets, but every one starts at zero and must pay the same stake and waiting cost as an honest agent. Influence peaks at the zenith only for identities with a long, checkable history, and voting weight is shaded in umber tiers by that history, so attacking means funding thousands of slow, expensive climbs instead of one cheap flood.
